source_evidence.observation: The source calls a random variable sub-exponential when it satisfies one of the equivalent properties (a)--(d) of Proposition 2.7.1.
The source denotes the sub-exponential norm by ||X||_{psi_1}, says it is 'the smallest K_3 in property 3,' and then says 'In other words' before displaying inf {t > 0 : E exp(|X|/t) <= 2}.
Properties (a)--(d) are stated to be equivalent up to an absolute constant factor: an absolute C makes property i with K_i imply property j with K_j <= C K_i for i,j=1,2,3,4.
Property (c) uses K_3 and requires E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda) for every 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3, whereas property (d) uses K_4 and is the one-point condition E exp(|X|/K_4) <= 2.
The immediately preceding exercise asks the reader to prove the equivalence of properties (a)--(d) in Proposition 2.7.1.

binders: A real-valued random variable X on an implicit probability space.
hypotheses: X satisfies at least one of the equivalent properties (a)--(d) in Proposition 2.7.1.
conclusions: X is called a sub-exponential random variable.
The sub-exponential norm of X is denoted ||X||_{psi_1}.
The printed prose says this norm is 'the smallest K_3 in property 3.'
Display (2.21), introduced by 'In other words,' gives ||X||_{psi_1} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(|X|/t) <= 2}.
definitions_and_conventions: Proposition 2.7.1 treats the four parameters in (a)--(d) as equivalent only up to an absolute constant factor, in the precise transfer sense stated in footnote 7.
Property (c), the third displayed property, has parameter K_3 and is a bounded-lambda estimate for the MGF of |X|.
Property (d), the fourth displayed property, has parameter K_4 and is the one-point exponential-moment bound E exp(|X|/K_4) <= 2.
The set in display (2.21) ranges over strictly positive scales t and uses the numerical threshold 2.
implicit_context: Probability, expectation, absolute value, and exponential are used in their standard real-valued random-variable sense.
No centering assumption is imposed for properties (a)--(d) or Definition 2.7.5.
The equivalence invoked by the definition is the absolute-factor equivalence of Proposition 2.7.1, not literal equality of its four parameters.

details: Membership in the sub-exponential class is characterized by satisfying any one of Proposition 2.7.1(a)--(d).
The displayed psi_1 quantity is the infimum of positive one-point exponential-moment scales with bound 2.
Absolute value is inside the exponential.
The prose literally says 'K_3 in property 3.'
This literal prose is distinct from display (2.21) and from Proposition 2.7.1(d), whose one-point parameter is K_4.

undebatable_constraints: The source classification uses the equivalent properties (a)--(d) of Proposition 2.7.1.
Display (2.21) takes an infimum over t > 0.
The integrand in display (2.21) is exp(|X|/t), with absolute value present.
The admissibility bound in display (2.21) is E exp(|X|/t) <= 2.
The printed 'property 3' wording must not be silently replaced by property (d) or K_4 when reporting the source, even though the display is the one-point condition associated with property (d).
No mean-zero hypothesis belongs to this definition.

ambiguities.issue: The norm prose has an apparent internal cross-reference mismatch.
ambiguities.evidence: Definition 2.7.5 says 'the smallest K_3 in property 3,' while Proposition 2.7.1(c), the third listed property, is the all-lambda bound with K_3; display (2.21) instead reproduces the one-point condition (d), whose proposition parameter is K_4.
ambiguities.impact: A faithfulness judgment must state whether it follows the literal K_3/property-3 prose, the explicit display (2.21), or property (d); equivalence up to an absolute factor does not make these parameterizations definitionally identical.

ambiguities.issue: The prose says 'smallest' while the displayed formula uses an infimum.
ambiguities.evidence: Both formulations occur consecutively in Definition 2.7.5, joined by 'In other words.'
ambiguities.impact: The source does not separately assert or prove attainment of the infimum here, so a formal minimum-attainment requirement would add content beyond the displayed equation.

contracts.contract_plain_english: A random variable is termed sub-exponential if it satisfies any of Proposition 2.7.1(a)--(d). Its psi_1 norm is displayed as the infimum of positive t for which E exp(|X|/t) is at most 2. The book's preceding prose literally calls this 'the smallest K_3 in property 3,' but that wording does not line up with the proposition labels: K_3 belongs to property (c), while the displayed one-point condition is property (d), parameterized there by K_4.

source_evidence.observation: The equation is ||X||_{psi_1} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(|X|/t) <= 2}.
The displayed equation occurs as the purported 'In other words' expansion of the prose saying the norm is the smallest K_3 in property 3.
The one-point condition underlying the display is E exp(|X|/K_4) <= 2.
The proposition's K_3 instead belongs to the bounded-lambda MGF condition E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda) for all 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3.

binders: A real-valued random variable X in the context of Definition 2.7.5.
A positive real scale t ranging over the admissible set inside the infimum.
hypotheses: In the inherited definition context, X satisfies one of the equivalent properties (a)--(d) and is therefore sub-exponential.
definitions_and_conventions: The admissible scales are strictly positive.
The one-point exponential moment uses |X|/t in the exponent and the threshold 2.
Proposition 2.7.1(d) states the same one-point shape using the positive parameter K_4.
implicit_context: Expectation is taken with respect to X's implicit probability law.
The equation appears within the definition of a sub-exponential random variable, so the preceding equivalence supplies at least one positive one-point scale.
The source does not specify a formal codomain or an empty-set convention for the infimum.

details: The condition is E exp(|X|/t) <= 2 at one point determined by t.
The display matches the mathematical shape of Proposition 2.7.1(d), not the bounded-lambda shape of property (c).
The preceding prose nevertheless literally names 'K_3 in property 3.'

undebatable_constraints: The left-hand side is the psi_1 norm of X.
The right-hand side is an infimum, not an asserted attained minimum.
The one-point condition of the display must be distinguished from Proposition 2.7.1(c)'s family of lambda-dependent bounds.

ambiguities.issue: Display (2.21) and its introductory prose point to differently labeled proposition properties.
ambiguities.evidence: The display is the one-point condition of property (d) with its scale renamed t, while the prose says 'K_3 in property 3,' and K_3/property (c) has a different all-lambda formula.
ambiguities.impact: The equation itself is explicit, but an implementation justified solely as 'property 3' must be checked against this source mismatch rather than treating the labels as interchangeable.

ambiguities.issue: The formal ambient type of the infimum is not stated in the prose.
ambiguities.evidence: Display (2.21) writes an ordinary infimum of positive real scales without specifying real versus extended-real conventions.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must choose an ambient infimum convention; any consequences of empty admissible sets or infinities are not explicit claims of this displayed equation, and the inherited sub-exponential context makes the admissible set nonempty.

contracts.contract_plain_english: Equation (2.21) defines the psi_1 norm as the infimum of positive scales t for which the single exponential moment E exp(|X|/t) is at most 2. This is the one-point condition displayed as Proposition 2.7.1(d), although the preceding prose literally refers to 'K_3 in property 3,' whose proposition formula is instead property (c).
